_comment: GATEC-CURVE. The Meadows chapter's progression curve, as data. One row per corridor region, in route order, each stating what the player's five are expected to BE when they arrive and what the region fields against them. Prompts 57 (team progression curve) and 67 (five-creature pressure) both asked for the chapter's curve to exist somewhere a later regional package can tune without reading GDScript; before this file it existed in three places, none of them tunable -- trainer levels scattered across five band directories, an expected-level model inside tools/_probe_pacing.py, and a CRITICAL_PATH constant inside a test file.
_comment_authority: This file does NOT own trainer teams (data/config/bands/<band>/trainers.json), wild populations (bands/<band>/spawns.json), the xp curve or the award (data/config/progression.json). It owns the BAND each of those must land inside, and tests/test_chapter_curve.gd fails the build when one drifts out. That split is deliberate: a regional package still authors its own content, it just cannot silently author it at the wrong strength for where it sits on the route.
_comment_measurement: The `team` bands are MEASURED, not wished for. `python3 tools/_probe_pacing.py` walks the shipped critical path against the shipped xp curve and award and prints, per band, the level a lead creature enters and leaves at. RE-MEASURED 2026-09-03 (G3-ECONOMY-0903): 3->9, 9->12, 12->15, 15->17, 17->21 (curve unchanged, still 40*L^1.15, award 30+16L). The 2026-08-22 numbers this comment used to record (3->8, 8->10, 10->13, 13->16, 16->20) were never a drift in the shipped content -- the probe itself was wrong the whole time and nobody had re-run it since. Two real bugs, both in tools/_probe_pacing.py, both fixed in the same pass: (1) its Band 1 critical path fought `trainer_oskar` for 'pays the South Bridge Key' and never fought the village tournament at all, but the 2026-08-22 TOURNAMENT-1 owner directive -- dated the SAME DAY as the stale measurement -- had already moved the bridge key off Oskar onto a Team Tether grunt (`south_bridge_grunt`) specifically so Oskar could become the tournament's final round, and `data/progression/objectives.json` gates the tracked objective chain on `tournament_won`, a flag only the tournament final writes, which makes the three-round tournament (`data/config/tournament.json`) mandatory critical path that the probe was silently skipping along with the real bridge fight. (2) `CATCHES_PER_BAND` charged the fourth catch to probe band 2 (chapter_curve region band2_stone_and_root) while this very file's own band1_lower_meadows row says 'the first four catches happen here' -- and the tournament's own `min_party_size: 5` entry gate sits inside band1_lower_meadows, before the bridge, so a player literally cannot reach the tournament board without all four catches done first. Both are now modeled; see tools/_probe_pacing.py's own comments at the fix sites. Re-run the probe after any tuning here or in progression.json; if the printed numbers move, these move with them.
_comment_measurement_pacing: The same corrected run also reprints the chapter's total-time verdict, which this file does not own but which every regional package should know: raw critical path 2.35h, projected first completion (the probe's own x2.0 floor multiplier) 4.71h against the 3-4h D42 target -- OVER, same verdict the old buggy probe also printed (4.74h). Fixing the tournament/bridge-grunt bug did not fix the pacing; it confirmed the OVER verdict was real rather than an artifact of the missing content. XP-curve/trainer-difficulty retuning to close that gap is Gate 4's charter (docs/ROADMAP.md), not this file's; recorded here so nobody reads a green Gate 3 curve as a green overall pace.
_comment_no_scaling: Prompt 57: 'The world does not rescale to the player.' Nothing in this file is read against the player's actual level. `wild_band` is resolved from a spawn's WORLD POSITION and nothing else -- a level-3 player who walks to the stronghold approach meets the same level 14-17 creatures a level-19 player does, and that is the point.
_comment_z_bands: `z_to` is the region's exclusive upper world-z bound, mirroring MEADOWS_MACRO_LAYOUT.md section 3's table and scripts/world/world_perimeter.gd's BAND*_Z1 constants exactly. tests/test_chapter_curve.gd asserts the two agree, because a corridor whose perimeter style changes at one z and whose creature strength changes at another would read as two different maps laid over each other. The last region's bound is deliberately far past the south cap so nothing can fall off the end of the table.

regions.name: Lower Meadows
regions.temptations: The first four catches happen here, so the five fills up here. Every later region's roster pressure is paid for by how attached the player got in this one.
regions.tuning: Wild band UNCHANGED from progression.json's historical global [2,6]: the opening is the most-tested stretch in the repo and the point of this file is not to reopen it. `expected_members` corrected 3 -> 5 (G3-ECONOMY-0903): this region's own `temptations` line already said the five fills up here, and `data/config/tournament.json`'s `entry.min_party_size: 5` is a real, wired gate inside this region, before the South Bridge -- a player cannot reach the tournament board with fewer than five. `exit` moved 8 -> 9: the tournament's three rounds and the real bridge gatekeeper (`south_bridge_grunt`, not `trainer_oskar`) are real Band 1 XP the old measurement never fought; see `_comment_measurement`.

regions.name: Stone & Root (Old Quarry / Burrow Warrens)
regions.temptations: Mudsnout's evolution gate (level 15 + bond 55 + a catalyst stone) is decided here even though it fires later -- this band names one of its two destinations (D71 added a second, band 5's Sunstone -> Ashtusk) -- and the Meadowhart met just past the South Bridge is the traversal slot arriving while the party is still filling.
regions.tuning: The field band tops out at 8, one below the Warrens' weakest resident: burrow_warrens.json's hand-placed levels (9, 10, 10, 11, guardian 14) sit strictly ABOVE the ridge outside on purpose -- a dungeon that fights at field strength is not a dungeon -- and tests/test_chapter_curve.gd fails the build if that ordering is ever lost. `trainer_levels` covers the warrens too, because it is this region's authored opposition; the band has no trainers of its own, which is prompt 59's gap, not this file's. `enter`/`expected_members` corrected 8/4 -> 9/5 (G3-ECONOMY-0903): the five is already full by the time Band 1's own tournament is entered (see that region's note), not partway through this one. Worth a look by whoever owns this band's spawns/trainers: the field band's own ceiling (8) now sits BELOW the team's corrected entry level (9), one level short of even matching it -- every wild creature here is already weaker than the team on arrival, not just by the time the band ends. Not changed here (`wild_band` drives live spawn rolls that BAND2 lanes are authoring content against right now); flagged for the coordinator to route.

regions.name: The River Lock (Tether Relay)
tools: second trait unlocks at full bond
regions.temptations: The five is normally full well before the relay is reached (Band 1's own tournament gate requires it), so a catch has cost somebody since the South Bridge. This is not the first region the cap bites -- it is the first region far enough into the chapter that a catch here is competing against real accumulated history, not just a full slot.
regions.tuning: The relay's four-fight ladder (8, 9, 10, 11-12) is the densest trainer run in the chapter and carries the player across this whole band on its own; the wild band exists to make a catch here a real alternative, not to be the xp source.

regions.name: Upper Meadows / Ironwood
regions.temptations: The Meadowhart cluster up here is the traversal creature met at a level that can actually fight, which is prompt 67's 'traversal must not create a dead slot' -- a mount picked up at level 2 in a level-14 region would have been exactly that dead slot.
regions.tuning: The corridor's longest single leg (Ironwood grove to the Sigil gate) so the ecology has room to vary without a wall. The 28-minute travel figure this note used to cite came from tools/_probe_pacing.py before its stale site coordinates were fixed; the leg measures ~7 minutes ridden. `enter` corrected 13 -> 15 (G3-ECONOMY-0903, see the file-level `_comment_measurement`): the corrected pacing probe's Band 1/3 fix compounds forward through every later band. Wild ceiling 14 -> 15 (W23-DIFFICULTY, CL-G8, D77): the corrected entry level is 15, and a field whose best creature is already a level under a team that has just arrived is not opposition on arrival. Widened from the TOP, the floor kept (D69's rule read for levels: the end that was right does not move) -- the band's floor 11 still gives a fresh arrival something beatable, and 15 stays under the region's exit (17) and under its captains (13-16). Band 2's identical finding is NOT applied: its ceiling is pinned at 8 by the Warrens' weakest resident (9), which must stay strictly above the field, and burrow_warrens.json is not this file's to move; the exact diff is in ralph/reports/W23-DIFFICULTY-0904/REPORT.md.

regions.name: Stronghold Approach & Meadows Hall
regions.temptations: The legendary join offer lands here against five creatures that have each been carried the length of the chapter. If a player can name a filler creature at this point, prompt 67 has failed upstream of the Hall, not in it. D71/T3-SUNSTONE adds a second one, cheaper to act on: the Sunstone sits in the scorched Team Tether ground by the Sigil gate, and a player who already has a bonded Mudsnout has to decide, in the same band that hands them the legendary offer, whether a SECOND Mudsnout raised from nothing is worth one of their five holders for an Ashtusk.
regions.tuning: Wild top (17) stays under the Warden's ace (20) and under the elite (19): the approach is drained, occupied land, not a place that out-levels the boss it leads to. `enter`/`exit` corrected 16/20 -> 17/21 (G3-ECONOMY-0903): the corrected probe still fights the Warden at L19, one below his ace, exactly as this note wants -- the exit figure (21) is the level AFTER his own team's xp is banked, a result of winning, not a pre-fight advantage. Nothing about 'stays under the ace' stopped being true; only the recorded arrival number was stale.

difficulty._comment: W23-DIFFICULTY (docs/decisions/D77). The chapter's BASELINE danger, as targets tests/smoke_combat_baseline.gd measures the shipped numbers against with a scripted pilot (attack on cooldown, chase, dodge nothing, no items) at each region's `team.enter` level. Owner-reproduced 2026-09-04: 'beating creatures and other trainers is way too easy'. Every value here is a target band, TUNABLE, and moving one is a decision to record, not a number to nudge until the smoke goes green. `party` is the typical five the pilot brings (the starter plus the four most-fielded Band 1 species); `potion_below_fraction` is the lead health under which a fight is scored as having needed a potion.
difficulty._comment_wild: An ordinary wild at band entry (the region's spawn table at the band's median level, count-weighted) costs the lead this fraction of its health -- a real dent that adds up over a leg and makes the camp worth reaching, never a wall. Band 1 is exempt: the opening meadow's [2,6] band is the most-tested stretch in the repo and its median wild out-levels the level-3 arrival by design (the tutorial reads it, the practice fight teaches it).
difficulty._comment_trainer_floor: The band's weakest non-gate trainer, fought unprepared by the whole party at the band's entry level, costs the LEAD this fraction of its health -- about half, so the next trainer in the band is a real question of rest, a potion or a switch (the smoke also prints how often a potion or a revive would be needed afterwards, `prep`, but with combat.json's 10% damage variance that rate is nearly binary per matchup and is reported, not asserted). This is D77's reading of the brief's 'lost one time in four without preparation'. It is NOT a full-five wipe rate: with the manager's auto-switch-on-faint a loss means five creatures down, and a band's WEAKEST trainer that wipes an equal-level five one run in four makes its strongest a wall and the tournament unwinnable at its own entry level. `min_win_rate` guards exactly that: the floor may hurt, it may not wall.
difficulty._comment_gates: The village tournament must stay winnable at its own `entry.min_level` (smoke_tournament_bracket.gd wins it); the Warden must stay winnable at the level the pacing probe says the team reaches him, and must cost the party no less than the elite before him (W-1). `max_single_hit_fraction` is G-3's fails-if: no profile's hit may take a full-health creature of the region's entry level in one blow, and 0.5 leaves the ace's telegraph a two-hit lesson rather than a one-hit one.

five_slot._comment: CLAUDE.md: five creatures total, no storage, no reserve, no sixth slot. Nothing here adds one. These are the numbers that decide whether the cap is a LIVE decision late in the chapter or a rule the player last thought about in hour one, and tests/test_chapter_curve.gd enforces each against the regions above.
five_slot._comment_deficit: How far below a region's expected team ENTRY level that region's strongest wild creature may sit before a catch there stops being a real option. This is the single number that decides whether the five-cap keeps biting: under the old single global [2,6] band, a creature caught in the stronghold approach arrived twelve levels below the team it was joining, so no player would ever weigh it against a member they had raised, so the cap silently stopped mattering after the first hour. A deficit of 2 means a fresh catch is always close enough to argue for.
five_slot._comment_options: More desirable creatures than slots is the whole mechanism. Six is the floor, not the target -- the roster is 25 species (3 starters, 2 evolution-only forms, and by all owner/decision references to date 1 legendary, so ~19 are ever wild-catchable candidates) and the spawn table currently fields 15 distinct non-starter ones (re-measured G3-ECONOMY-0903; this comment previously said 17/12, both stale against WORLD-CONTENT/BAND1-ECOLOGY's species additions since it was written). Per-region: band1_lower_meadows 11, band2_stone_and_root 6, band3_the_river_lock 14, band4_upper_meadows_ironwood 8, band5_stronghold_approach 7 (chapter_curve region boundaries, `python3 -c` one-liner against spawns.json + this file's own `z_to` table; a player meets several times the floor before the Hall in every region past the opening). Asserted against the merged spawn table so deleting a species from the world fails the build instead of quietly making the cap free.
five_slot._comment_costs: What the player actually loses by replacing a member, all of it already implemented and none of it storage: invested levels (progression.json's curve is steep enough that a mid-chapter replacement starts several fights behind), accumulated bond and its stat nodes plus the second trait it unlocks at full bond, Best Creature designation, an in-progress evolution gate, and the traversal slot if the one being cut is the mount. The release ceremony (R4.10) is where those are shown before the choice is committed.
